In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of a novel GH27 enzyme that can catalyze the efficient synthesis of globotrialose.
the identification and characterization of a new α-galactose-specific glycosyltransferase, which is the first α-galacto-synthase that has been reported in the genus Bacteroides.
the efficient and regioselectivity synthesis of globotrioside by the recombinant α-galactohydrolase AgaBfS3.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AgaBfS is a promising biocatalyst for the efficient and regioselectivity synthesis of globotrios.
AgaBfS3 is the first α-galactobiosidase that can catalyze the synthesis of globotrioside.
AgaBfS3 is a novel and efficient α-galactohydrolase and a promising candidate for the synthesis of globotriosyl-containing oligosaccharide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned, characterized, and applied the AgaBf gene from Bacteroidetes for the first time to synthesize the important glycoconjugate globotriose.
we have successfully developed a novel one-enzyme one-pot synthetic method for the synthesis of globotrisose from pNPαGAL and lactose by AgaB3fS.

we have developed a novel α-glycosidase AgaBf2S from Bacteroidetes that can efficiently catalyze the regioselective transfer of galactosyl from pNPαGAL to lactose to produce a single product of Galα1–3Galβ1–3Glc, which is the core structure of SSEA4.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AgaBf enzyme is a novel glycosidase that can be used to produce the important glycan globotriose.
AgaBfS can be used to synthesize globotriosyl glycosides with high regioselectivity and efficiency.
AgaBfS can catalyze the synthesis of globotrioside with high efficiency and α1–4 selectivity.
